hook.text: Political ads spend more money on negative attacks than positive messages. Fear wins elections.

buildup.text: Election propaganda uses simplification, fear, and emotional appeals to influence voters.

discovery.text: The 'Willie Horton' ad in 1988 used racial fear to destroy a presidential candidate's lead.

twist.text: Negative ads work even when voters say they hate them — the emotional impact sticks.

climax.text: Modern micro-targeting delivers different propaganda to different voters based on their psychology.

punchline.text: The ad you see isn't the ad your neighbor sees.

quiz.question: Why do negative political ads work despite being disliked?
options: The emotional impact sticks regardless of stated preferences
